back: The addition to the environment of substances or energy (noise, heat, light) in amounts that harm living things or reduce environmental quality.
Point: one identifiable outlet (a pipe). Non-point: spread over an area (fertiliser runoff, traffic exhaust).
Nutrient enrichment of water causes algal blooms; decay of the algae uses up oxygen, killing fish.
Temperature, pH, turbidity and E. coli; drinking water should contain no E. coli in 100 mL.
Water, land, air, noise and visual.
Domestic, construction, manufacturing and power, transport and waste.
LICs: untreated sewage, open burning. MICs: rapid industry and traffic, weak controls. HICs: cleaner but high waste and traffic emissions.
Zimbabwe's Environmental Management Act (Chapter 20:27) sets standards for waste and effluent and applies the polluter-pays principle.
Judge each measure by cost, ease of enforcement and whether it tackles the cause or only the symptom.
